title: POC workshop facilitation template - rapid alignment & deployment mapping
content:
Goal: Run a 90-minute customer workshop that produces an agreed POC scope, success criteria, and a first-cut deployment proposal (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with owners and next steps.

Audience: Customer product + infra leads, Redwood SE lead, Redwood infra specialist (if private/dedicated is likely), customer data owner (if using private data). Limit to 6-9 total participants for productive discussion.

Pre-work (to send 3 business days before):
- One-page intake form from customer: main user flows, data sensitivity, target latency/cost goals, anticipated QPS.
- Short tech checklist: does the customer have a VPC? KMS? preferred cloud region?
- Sample prompt set (5-10 examples) + 10 representative documents (if retrieval needed).
- Quick read: 2-page options brief comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private (attached).

Room setup and logistics:
- Video + 2 screens (slides + live demo terminal).
- Shared Google Doc open for notes and action items.
- Recording allowed only with customer consent.

90-minute agenda (timeboxed):
1) 0-10m — Welcome & objectives (SE lead): set success criteria for the workshop, align on scope (POC user flow), confirm attendees and roles.
2) 10-25m — Customer context + demo of current flow (Customer PM): pain points, metrics, current infra. SE to capture constraints.
3) 25-40m — Quick architecture options walkthrough (SE): three options (hosted API, dedicated reserved pool, private/VPC) mapped to customer constraints. Use decision criteria matrix (latency, cost, compliance, data residency).
4) 40-55m — Live model demo & profiling (SE infra): run representative prompt set on the candidate model using a short latency/cost probe; show token-level timing and cost estimate.
5) 55-70m — Breakout: mapping the POC (small groups or whole-team whiteboard). Deliverable: one-page POC charter (goal, success metrics, test harness, timeline, infra choice).
6) 70-80m — Report back & alignment on success criteria (facilitator captures consensus).
7) 80-90m — Next steps, owners, and date for POC kickoff; capture risks and mitigating actions.

Slide outline (12 slides + appendix) with speaker notes:
- Slide 1: Title + workshop objectives (SE lead). Speaker note: keep objectives explicit and measurable.
- Slide 2: Attendees & roles (one slide to call out decision owners).
- Slide 3: Customer context summary (PM). Note: highlight 3 pain points.
- Slide 4: Proposed user flow for the POC (diagram). Note: show where LLM sits and data ingress/egress.
- Slide 5: Options comparison (hosted / dedicated / private) — decision criteria table.
- Slide 6: Baseline performance profile (results from pre-profiling + expected SLOs).
- Slide 7: Cost-back-of-envelope for target QPS and SLO. Show assumptions.
- Slide 8: Security & compliance checklist relevant to each option.
- Slide 9: POC test plan & success metrics (functional + non-functional). Use PASS/FAIL thresholds.
- Slide 10: Roles & responsibilities (customer vs Redwood).
- Slide 11: Timeline & milestones (2-8 week POC options).
- Slide 12: Risks, dependencies, and contingency plan.
- Appendix: sample prompts, evaluation harness, infra checklist, access checklist.

Facilitation notes and micro-scripts:
- Opening: "We have 90 minutes; by the end we want an executable POC charter with owners and a recommended infra approach."
- When tension arises (e.g., customer asks for production-level SLAs now): use timebox: "Let's capture that as a production ask — for the POC our objective is collect data and validate feasibility. We will surface SLA asks to the sales/enterprise team after this session."
- To draw a decision: "Based on the matrix, which option would you prefer to validate first? If we're undecided, let's pick the lowest-effort path that still validates your primary risk (latency / privacy / scale)."
- Parking lot pattern: have a running bullet list on the shared doc under "parking lot" for items that need separate conversations (contracting, legal review, long-term cost optimization).

POC charter template (one-page fields to capture during breakout):
- POC name (short):
- Business objective (quantified):
- Primary user flow to validate (step-by-step, 3–6 steps):
- Success metrics (primary + secondary; include exact thresholds):
- Candidate model(s) + quantization/latency knobs:
- Infra choice and rationale: hosted / dedicated / private (specific config if known):
- Data access pattern and security controls required:
- Timeline (start date, length, key milestones):
- Test harness & sample prompts/datasets:
- Owners (customer lead, customer infra, Redwood SE lead, Redwood infra):
- Acceptance criteria & sign-off gate: Yes/No and who signs.

Technical prep checklist for Redwood infra prior to kickoff:
- Access credentials for customer test data (if needed) or synthetic data prepared.
- Region selected and expected latency target.
- Model artifact(s) staged in test bucket; quantized variants if applicable.
- Basic infra terraform/workspace scaffold ready for hosted/dedicated/private variants.
- Observability hooks inserted: token-level timing, trace IDs, cost counters.

Sample evaluation metrics and how to present them (quick bullets):
- Latency: p50/p95 for candidate prompt set, measured end-to-end.
- Cost: $/k token estimate for baseline QPS assumptions.
- Quality: accuracy/ROUGE/F1 or customer-defined satisfaction score on 50 labeled examples.
- Reliability: error rate (5xx/timeout) under target QPS during a short load test.

Facilitator checklist (on the day):
- Mute participants only when necessary; encourage short clarifying questions.
- Keep breakout to 15 minutes maximum.
- Capture decisions inline with action owner and due date.
- Take a screenshot of the architecture whiteboard and paste into the shared doc.

Common workshop traps & how to avoid them:
- Trap: discussion collapses into long-term architecture debates.
  Avoidance: reframe as "For the POC we need the smallest scope that tests the key risk."
- Trap: customer expects production cost numbers.
  Avoidance: provide a range and explicate assumptions; mark cost optimizations as a follow-up workstream.
- Trap: legal/compliance questions pause momentum.
  Avoidance: capture the questions, map to specific docs (DPA, SOC2 evidence), and propose a legal sync after the POC kickoff.

Example prompts (for retrieval or generation tests):
- Prompt type: instruction -> expected output
- Example 1: "Summarize the following support ticket into a 2-line triage note and priority (high/medium/low): [ticket body]" -> expected: 2-line summary + priority label.
- Example 2: "Given this product spec, generate 5 release-test scenarios focusing on edge cases." -> expected: numbered list, each with 1 sentence description.

Post-workshop deliverables (within 48 hours):
- Completed one-page POC charter (PDF) with owners and dates.
- Short recording excerpt (if recorded) and 1-page decisions & risks summary.
- Lightweight runbook for Redwood infra to spin up POC environment (link to repo).

Acceptance & escalation path:
- If POC fails to meet primary success metric: triage meeting within 3 business days to determine root cause and next steps (retry, adjust model/hyperparams, expand data, or pivot infra).

Notes for SEs doing this the first time:
- Focus on measurable outcomes, not perfect architecture. The POC's job is to de-risk the biggest unknown quickly.
- Keep customer involved in test design — they must own success metrics.
- Use the decision matrix to make the infra choice explicit and defensible.

Appendix (short references):
- Quick link to template repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-templates
- Example POC charter (anonymized): (attached in Drive)
- Contact: asha.patel@redwood.ai (SE lead)
